work.title: Trauer-Cantate, bey Gelegenheit des am 19 Decemb. 1751 erfolgten Absterben der Königinn und Frauen, Louise

history.p: When Queen Louise died in December 1751, the court officials led by Lord Chamberlain Adam Gottlob Moltke started planning the funeral. It is reasonable to assume that music was required for the event and that an author was ordered to write the text and a composer requested to set it to music. However, so far no clear evidence has been found proving that a cantata was indeed performed though it is implied in the instructions which Moltke gave. The present cantata was composed for the commemoration of the queen and performed at The Musical Society on 3 February 1752. Though the printed text neither indicates author nor composer, it seems likely that Scheibe must have had a hand in it, since Paolo Scalabrini, who was the acting Kapellmeister at the time, would not have been able to write a Lutheran cantata to a German text. Another possible candidate is Peder Sparkiær though he only wrote Danish texts, and Thomas Clitau seems unlikely. According to the newspapers the author was German. The cantata consists of two parts (in order to have been performed at the funeral service it would need three parts) and the length of the text suggests that the work must have been quite extensive which does not agree with Scheibe’s other cantatas for similar events; on the other side, in his Abhandlung vom Ursprunge und Alter der Musik published in 1776 (SchW C1:001), Scheibe mentions having composed a mourning cantata which was indeed performed at The Musical Society. The text book does not reveal information on the number of singers.

incipText.p: Wiewohl ist mir der Kampf gelungen!
Ich habe einen guten Kampfs gekämpfet
Nun bleibt, was sterblich war, zurücke
Mein Glaube hat mir manchen Sieg
Doch es ist nicht so leicht
Hinfort ist mir beygelegt die Krone der Gerechtigkeit
Du glänzest heller als die Sonne
Das Denkmahl Deiner Huld und Güte
Dich hatte Glück, Geburt und Stand
Gott weiß allein, wodurch auf Erden
Nun ruhe sanft in Deiner Gruft
Louise! schlafe wohl und sanft in deinem Grabe
Folgt nun auf wohl beschloßnen Kampf
Wer an mich gläubet, der wird leben
